newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Theresa in intensive care after fall.
newsitem.headline: Mother Theresa in intensive care after fall.

text.p: Mother Teresa was rushed to hospital on Monday after falling and hurting her head, hospital officials and an aide said.

The Roman Catholic nun was taken to the intensive cardiac care unit of Woodlands Nursing Home in this eastern Indian city after she fell down at Mother House, the headquarters of her Missionaries of Charity religious order.
A nun told Reuters that Mother Teresa appeared dazed for about 10 minutes after the fall before being taken to hospital.

The Press Trust of India (PTI) said Mother Teresa, 86, fell from her bed in the afternoon and injured her right eye. The news agency said the injury was not serious but she underwent a brain scan at the hospital.
"Mother can see well and is keeping fine," PTI quoted a doctor as saying.
The Nobel Peace laureate recently spent 18 days in the same hospital with heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia. She spent most of the time on a respirator.
Known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and destitute, Mother Teresa was released on September 6, but doctors advised her to rest in bed.
Mother Teresa, who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1979, was fitted with a cardiac pacemaker in 1989.

In 1991, she was treated at a Californian hospital for heart disease and bacterial pneumonia. Two years later she fell in Rome and broke three ribs. In August 1993, she developed malaria, complicated by heart and lung problems. Last April she fractured her left collar bone.
The Missionaries of Charity, which she founded in 1949, runs some 544 homes for unwanted children and the destitute in more than 80 cities.
The work includes caring for nearly 7,000 children in 120 homes and arranging 1,500 adoptions each year.
